title: partial-region-microburst-warm-standby-orchestration-notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working set of notes capturing the detection, mitigation, short-term fixes, and recommended runbook changes after a partial-region microburst that manifested as asymmetric latency and token-rate saturation in eu-west-1 edge POPs on 2026-02-09. The event did not require full region failover but exposed gaps in our warm-standby choreography, DNS TTL handling, and KV cache pre-seeding logic.

High-level impact:
- Time window: ~2026-02-09T10:07Z to 2026-02-09T11:45Z (primary spike with intermittent recovery blips until 11:45).
- Customer-facing impact: increased P50->P99 latencies for hosted API routes serving heavy-chat workloads; a handful of vanity customers saw 10-30% elevated error rates due to timeouts at our edge proxies.
- Traffic pattern: concentrated on eu-west-1 edge POPs, ~2.2x baseline token/sec for a 12-minute microburst period followed by sustained 1.2x for 45 minutes. Backend compute capacity nominal.

Detection timeline (concise):
- 10:06: alert: route-level latency spike from EU edge probes (synthetic). Alert flagged by probe aggregation rule.
- 10:07: on-call pager for eng-sre triggered. Initial triage: edge latency with 502/504s at proxies.
- 10:10: Observability: tracing shows large queueing delay at edge proxy -> router hop. Upstream model servers did not report CPU/GPU saturation.
- 10:15: KV cache hit-rate dropped by 40% for common prefixes from eu region. Pre-seeded keys in warm region were not leveraged due to routing policy sticking to local POPs.
- 10:23: Engineering hypothesis: control-plane signal misrouting + DNS TTL caching at CDN causing clients to continue hitting degraded POPs even after partial routing adjustment.
- 10:36: Manual weighted traffic shift initiated (30% to warm standby region) via routing console. TTL propagation lag observed.
- 10:49: Automated fallback policies started to route to alternate model variants, reducing errors.
- 11:10: Full 50% shift applied, cold-start latency increase noticed in some model variants (lack of pre-warmed caches).
- 11:45: Traffic returned to normal; post-incident monitoring window kept until 12:30.

Root causes (probable, prioritized):
1) Edge-level transient overload (microburst) at POPs that primarily impacts proxy queueing, not model servers. The spike exceeded in-flight request thresholds causing proxy timeouts.
2) Warm-standby orchestration assumed DNS-based routing controls + short TTLs; in practice CDN and client-side caches respected longer TTLs causing stale local routing to continue post-shift.
3) KV cache pre-seeding for warm-standby was incomplete: key prefixes used by chat sessions were missing in standby region leading to cold KV lookups and cold model variant paths (higher latency).
4) Observability gaps: lack of a clear fused signal combining queueing latency, KV hit-rate, and DNS propagation to trigger faster automated shift.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Increase proxy request queue limit and temporarily raise per-POP connection backpressure thresholds (rolled back after 90 minutes).
- Manual weighted routing shift via console to eu-central-1 warm standby; applied in 3 stages (30% -> 50% -> 100% fallback possible but stopped at 50% due to cold-starts).
- Enabled model-variant fallback logic earlier in the chain to reduce error responses where requests timed out.
- Telemetry patch to surface KV cache hit-rate per POP in the real-time dashboard.

Observed tradeoffs and side effects:
- Manual shifting reduced errors but increased tail latency for some customers due to cold KV/model start in standby region.
- Raising proxy queue sizes increased memory pressure on proxies but avoided client-visible 5xx for the time-window.

Runbook gaps identified (actionable to update):
- DNS/TTL checklist: add explicit steps to invalidate/flush CDN caches when initiating a regional shift; include client-targeted guidance for partners with long TTLs.
- Warm-standby pre-seed validation: require pre-seed verification step (check-sum of critical KV prefixes) before shifting >25% traffic.
- Shift ramp policy: define min-step windows (e.g., wait 6 minutes between adjustments) and automated rollback criteria (error rate spike >5% absolute or P95 latency increase >200ms).
- Orchestration triggers: add a fused SLO-aligned composite signal (queueing depth + KV-hit-rate + DNS error rate) to automatically trigger the first shift step.

Suggested short-term fixes (0-2 weeks):
- Implement a CDN cache-invalidation API call in the routing console as a pre-shift option. Owner: Priya (routing). Due: 2026-02-23.
- Add KV pre-seed verification job that runs hourly and reports delta. Owner: Ethan (infra-kv). Due: 2026-02-20.
- Create a synthetic canary that simulates client TTL behavior (long TTL/short TTL) to observe propagation in a staged shift. Owner: Jonah (sre-observability). Due: 2026-02-24.

Medium-term changes (2-8 weeks):
- Implement composite auto-trigger for shallow traffic shift (first 25%) using the fused signal above. Add experiment to test auto-shift on simulated microbursts. Owner: eng-sre + serving-runtime. Due: 2026-03-30.
- Update warm-standby documentation to specify pre-warm thresholds for KV and model caches (target 95% pre-warm hit-rate for critical prefixes). Owner: product-ops + infra. Due: 2026-03-15.

Checklist for next on-call runbook iteration (add these as discrete steps):
1) Triage: verify whether overload is POP-local or region-wide (metric queries provided below).
2) If POP-local: enable proxy queue expansion (short-lived flag) and notify CDN partners.
3) Verify KV pre-seed checksum for warm standby for affected prefixes.
4) Initiate staged weighted shift: 30% -> observe 6m -> 50% -> observe 12m -> 75% -> 100% only if pre-warm hit-rates are stable.
5) Trigger CDN cache invalidation immediately after first shift step.
6) If cold-start tail latency > 400ms at P95 after shift, rollback to previous weight and wait for pre-warm job to complete.

Useful queries and probes (copy these into runbook playbook):
- Edge queue depth per-POP: SELECT percentile(queue_depth, 95) FROM edge_proxy WHERE region = 'eu-west-1' AND time > now() - 15m
- KV pre-seed hit-rate: metric(kv.preseed.hit_rate) by region, prefix
- DNS TTL variance: histogram(dns.response_ttl) by cdn_provider, region over last 1h
- Client resolvers honoring TTLs: synthetic probe that resolves domain, caches for 10m, then resolves again to detect discrepancy

Open questions and follow-ups:
- How many customers have long-lived client TTLs that ignore our TTL hints? (Engineering to survey top-50 vanity customers). Owner: solutions-engineering. Due: 2026-02-26.
- Can we combine pre-seed and model warm start into a single orchestration hook to reduce cold-starts? (Research needed). Owner: applied-ml + infra. Due: 2026-03-12.
- Should we add an explicit CDN-agnostic 'immediate reroute' flag that bypasses TTL expectations for emergency shifts? Pros/cons to discuss with legal and partners. Owner: product-hosted-api. Due: 2026-03-01.

Postmortem actions (short list to mark as tracked tasks):
- SRE-2104: implement pre-seed verification + reporting (Ethan).
- SRE-2105: add CDN invalidation capability to routing console (Priya).
- SRE-2106: build synthetic TTL probe and add dashboard (Jonah).
- SRE-2107: draft updated warm-standby runbook with explicit step timings and rollback criteria (Asha).

Notes to self / informal observations (keep for team context):
- The microburst highlighted that we assume clients follow our routing hints more than they actually do. Any plan that relies solely on DNS TTLs to move traffic is brittle.
- Pre-warming for model-serving is reasonably well-handled for Reserved capacity but our warm-standby path needs more deterministic verification.
- Communication: customers saw increased tail but only a few reported incidents — implies our automated retries/fallbacks prevented broader failures. We should still proactively reach out to top affected accounts with mitigation notes.

Next sync: schedule 30m post-incident review with infra-kv, routing, applied-ml, and SRE to align on owners and timelines. Proposed slot: 2026-02-19 16:00 UTC.

Appendix (quick copy-paste snippets to include in runbook updates):
- Default short shift ramp: 30% -> wait 6m -> 50% -> wait 12m -> 75% -> wait 18m -> 100%
- Rollback triggers: absolute error-rate increase > 3% (5xx), P95 latency increase > 200ms, KV hit-rate drop > 20% post-shift.
- Pre-seed verification steps (short): pull list of critical prefixes -> compute checksum -> compare to standby -> report delta -> if delta > 5% then run async pre-seed job and delay >25% shift.

End of notes. Will convert into a formal runbook PR and SRE postmortem once owners confirm timelines.
